sessions.title: App boots and shows data
sessions.goal: Serve the seeded expenses and render them as a table with a per-payer totals section.

criteria.check: GET /api/expenses returns 200 with a JSON array of Expense (every item has integer amountCents)
sc-expenses renders one row per expense (count of data-testid=expense-row equals the number of seeded expenses)
sc-expenses renders per-payer totals (data-testid=payer-total-<name>) with each payer's total equaling the sum of their paid amountCents

cuts.hint: Put every seeded expense into `body` and set `status` to 200
Fetch "/api/expenses", parse the JSON, and write the resulting array into `expenses`
Group the loaded expenses by payer and write each payer’s summed amount in cents into `totals`

sessions.title: Netting works
sessions.goal: Compute per-person net balances and propose a naive greedy settlement; render the proposed transfers list.
teaches: Pure functions at a server boundary

criteria.check: GET /api/settlement returns 200 with balances whose deltas (paid minus owed) match the seeded fixture in integer cents
GET /api/settlement includes a transfers array whose amounts sum to zero and whose totals match balances for each person (greedy proposal)
GET /api/settlement returns transfers sorted deterministically by from, then to, ascending
sc-expenses shows the section title 'Proposed transfers' when settlement data is loaded

cuts.hint: For the given expenses and participants, compute each person’s net cents (paid minus an equal share by weight) and write the mapping into `out`
Using the balances mapping, greedily match the largest creditor with the largest debtor until all deltas are zero and write the list of transfers into `out`
Compute balances and transfers for the current request and write both into `body` with `status` set to 200; sort `body.transfers` deterministically by from, then to ascending
Fetch "/api/settlement", parse the JSON, and write the object into `settlement`

sessions.title: Minimal transfers and rounding
sessions.goal: Refine the settlement to reduce the number of transfers while preserving totals, keep output deterministic, add an include/exclude toggle and integer-safe formatting.
teaches: UI toggle state and query parameters

criteria.check: GET /api/settlement on the seed yields a transfers list length equal to the refined minimal strategy and in a deterministic sequence
GET /api/settlement?include=<subset> excludes omitted people (no transfer mentions an excluded name) and transfers still balance to zero
sc-expenses include/exclude toggle recomputes the transfers list without a full page reload (toggling a person off removes any transfer involving them)
sc-expenses renders, for each transfer-row, a transfer amount element (data-testid=transfer-amount) whose text equals the currency string for that row's integer cents (e.g., $12.34)
sc-expenses renders one row per transfer (count of data-testid=transfer-row equals the number of transfers from the settlement endpoint)

cuts.hint: Refine the settlement so `out` contains a transfer set with the same totals but fewer payments than the naive greedy result, using tie-breaking that keeps a deterministic person-order
Format an integer cents value into `out` as a currency string like "$12.34" without using floating-point rounding
Maintain the set of included people in `included` and update it when a toggle is clicked, then trigger a reload of the settlement using the include list
Parse the request’s include query into the set `included` and apply it so only those people participate in balances and transfers
Build the array of renderable rows for the transfers list from `settlement.transfers` and write it into `rows`
